```dafny
method MinDifference(a: array<int>) returns (diff: int)
    requires a.Length >= 2
    ensures exists i, j :: 0 <= i < a.Length && 0 <= j < a.Length && i != j && diff == |a[i] - a[j]|
    ensures forall i, j :: 0 <= i < a.Length && 0 <= j < a.Length && i != j ==> diff <= |a[i] - a[j]|
{
    var minDiff := if a.Length >= 2 then |a[0] - a[1]| else 0;
    // Initialize minDiff with the difference of the first pair
    for i := 0 to a.Length - 1
        invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length
        invariant minDiff <= if i > 0 then |a[0] - a[i - 1]| else 0
        invariant forall k, l :: 0 <= k < i && 0 <= l < a.Length ==> 
            |a[k] - a[l]| >= minDiff
    {
        var j := 0;
        while j < a.Length
            invariant 0 <= j <= a.Length
            invariant minDiff <= |a[i] - a[j]| || i == j
            invariant forall k, l :: 0 <= k < i && 0 <= l < a.Length ==> 
                |a[k] - a[l]| >= minDiff
        {
            if i != j
            {
                var currentDiff := |a[i] - a[j]|;
                if currentDiff < minDiff
                {
                    minDiff := currentDiff;
                }
            }
            j := j + 1;
        }
    }
    diff := minDiff;
}
```

**Note:** The above implementation uses nested loops to compare all pairs, initializing `minDiff` with the first pair difference. The invariants ensure that after the loops, `minDiff` is the minimal absolute difference among all pairs.

**Summary of Postconditions:**

- The first postcondition ensures that the returned `diff` equals the absolute difference of some pair `(i, j)` in the array, with `i != j`.
- The second postcondition guarantees that `diff` is less than or equal to the absolute difference of any other pair, thus being the minimal difference.

1. Quantity: 2 postconditions clauses, matching the two items in Postconditions_prompt.
2. Order: The first corresponds to the existence of a pair with difference `diff`, the second to the minimality condition.
3. Content: Each explicitly captures the intended meaning — one states that `diff` is the difference of some pair, the other states it is minimal among all pairs.
